newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African named for world tourism post.
newsitem.headline: S.African named for world tourism post.

text.p: Former South African environment minister Dawie de Villiers has been selected for the post of deputy secretary general of the World Tourism Organisation, the government said in a statement on Monday.
He will begin the four-year assignment at the 128-member organisation's Madrid headquarters in October.

De Villiers, a National Party veteran and minister of environment affairs and tourism during the first two years of President Nelson Mandela's government of national unity, was chosen by the organisation's executive committee to succeed Francesco Fragialli.
Frangialli was elected secretary general, but his post had to be ratified at a full meeting of the organisation in Istanbul in October, de Villiers said in an interview.

He said the World Tourism Organisation, funded mainly by membership fees and project-related United Nations grants, maintained a global database, promoted tourism around the world and offered members planning and strategic advice.
"Tourism is a major industry throughout the world, but it is fragmented. Many countries need and will benefit from the infrastructure that the World Tourism Organisation offers," he said.

"The majority of the projects are designed to assist developing countries, but the organisation also does a lot of research, for instance on the taxation of tourism, which is of benefit to developed countries as well," he said.
De Villiers said he would resign his parliamentary seat before October.
